name: Salvador Allende
role: President of Chile (1970–1973); Socialist Party founder and senator
summary: Chilean physician and Marxist Socialist Party leader who won the presidency in 1970 at the head of the Unidad Popular coalition and pursued a 'Chilean road to socialism' through elections, constitutional channels and pluralism. His government nationalised copper and banks, expanded agrarian reform and planning, and defended national sovereignty against foreign corporations, while he insisted on legality and civil liberties; he died during the 11 September 1973 military coup.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The Unidad Popular program he presented promised medical and dental care for all Chileans financed by the state, employers and social insurance, with free hospital medicines.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Program called for statutory 'vital' and minimum wages that actually cover needs, with automatic cost-of-living adjustments; his government signed a wage accord with the CUT and raised pay in 1971.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Told the UN that production should respond to social needs and not individual profit, and the program puts a planning system and state-dominated economic area in place of market allocation.

public-ownership.rationale: Program and his government nationalised copper, nitrate, iron, coal, banking and foreign trade and placed electricity, rail, air and sea transport, oil and steel in a dominant public sector.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: In his 1973 message he said the bills sent to Congress proposed taxing the highest-income sectors, 'as is just', alongside a campaign against tax evasion.

unions-good.rationale: Program guaranteed unionisation and the right to strike and extended it to groups lacking it; he signed an agreement with the CUT naming the unions partners in government policy.

property-fundamental.rationale: Program expropriated monopolies and large estates, and he said he would end private property wherever it harms others, keeping it only for homes, cars and small firms.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Program promised to end monopolies and subject foreign capital to conditions; at the UN he denounced transnationals as unaccountable to any parliament and called for international study and control.

cut-welfare.rationale: Program and his government expanded social security, family allowances, free school meals and milk; he framed dependency as a result of capitalist structure, not of benefits.

worker-ownership.rationale: In March 1972 he called it dangerous and demagogic to tell workers they would own the firms: workers would administer enterprises while the Chilean people owned them.

strong-leader.rationale: Program rejected 'dictatorial presidentialism' and defined a strong government as one resting on organised popular support, not coercion; he refused to override Congress and promised never to seek reelection.

state-harmful.rationale: His project was to build a state-led economy and a new state in which workers hold power, not to dispense with the state.

empower-police-military.rationale: Program promised the armed forces proper materials and fair pay, but also disbanded the riot police unit and reorganised the police so they could not repress the people.

decide-locally.rationale: Program promised administrative decentralisation and local organs of power with economic and political powers, but bound them to national laws and national economic plans.

rehabilitation.rationale: Program said the prison regime must be transformed from the root with a view to regeneration and recovery of offenders.

traditional-family.rationale: Called the family the essential nucleus of society and created a family protection ministry in the program, yet said family life is a myth for many poor households and backed divorce and equal status of all children.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Program promised secure land and credit for the Mapuche and other indigenous peoples; his government sent a bill restoring usurped lands to the Mapuche.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Program set national values against 'cultural colonisation' as an aim of education and popular culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Said socialist change needs intermediate phases and respect for legality, institutions and a long process, while aiming at a revolutionary transformation of the system.

free-trade.rationale: Program put foreign trade under state control and he criticised deteriorating terms of trade and the world economic order, though he also denounced barriers to selling Chilean raw materials.

limit-growth.rationale: Program set rapid, decentralised economic growth that maximises productive forces as an objective.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Hoped for an atomic reactor to desalinate water and supply power in northern Chile, and strengthened the Nuclear Energy Commission.

revolution-justified.rationale: Described his government's aim as a revolution, said revolutionary struggle may be the guerrilla focus, the armed wing or the electoral road, and said that if legal roads were closed armed insurgency would remain.

experts-over-public.rationale: Said education reform must be decided and carried out by teachers, workers, students and parents and 'not only by technicians', and gave workers a central role in planning.

central-planning.rationale: Program put a binding national planning system with executive decisions at the centre of a state-dominated economy, but kept a private sector and a mixed area.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Program had the state area and national planning direct investment, and his government set up joint CUT-ODEPLAN planning of production and investment in the social area.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Program protected small and medium owners, set every family owning its home and organised cooperatives, while concentrating large industry in the state.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: He signed an accord creating a tripartite government-worker-employer wage commission, yet insisted that classes have antagonistic interests and rejected the Christian Democrats' 'communitarian' third way.

one-party-rule.rationale: Called a single party unreal, formed a multiparty government, and said nobody, himself included, would accept one party's hegemony.

democracy-best.rationale: Insisted socialism be built through elections, pluralism and constitutional channels, but distinguished 'authentic' democracy from formal democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Held that disputes with Congress and a new constitution could be settled by a plebiscite and called the plebiscite a legitimate constitutional weapon.

workers-councils.rationale: Program wanted a single People's Assembly as supreme organ and on 1 May 1973 he said popular power organs and cordones must not become a power parallel to the government and the CUT.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said revolutionary violence is the answer to reactionary violence and that if the legal roads were closed armed insurgency was possible.

war-builds-character.rationale: Said peoples like Chile struggle for peace, not war, and championed disarmament and the end of the arms race.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Program set out a state system of justice with an independent judiciary, state police and national defence as a duty of the whole people.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Said the Chilean people took the revolutionary road without forgetting the fundamental Marxist principle of class struggle, and called Marxism a method of interpreting history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Called for an equal starting point and an end to first- and second-class citizens, but said nobody can equalise all people and that arrival depends on each, while his program redistributed income sharply.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Program promised to defend Mapuche and other indigenous communities against usurpation and secure their lands and democratic self-direction.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Program contrasts fraternity with individualism, and his 1971 message hoped for a society without war of all against all in economic competition.

restore-past-order.rationale: Described his task as transforming the legal, social and economic order of the past into a socialist one.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Called doctrine a guide to action not a dogma and denounced sectarianism, but stayed committed to socialism as the goal.

direct-action.rationale: Held that change would come by elections and legal reform, criticised seizures of farms and plants, and said illegal land takeovers do not help agrarian reform.

means-match-ends.rationale: Said the Chilean road should build 'the first socialist society on a democratic, pluralist and libertarian model' and avoid authoritarian forms of government during the transition.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred: he wanted rapid industrial development, science and technology to end hunger and underdevelopment, which excludes a return to foraging.

production-for-use.rationale: Told the UN that economic democracy means productive activity answers needs and social expectations and not private profit; program turned industry toward popular consumer goods.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Said the old structure rests on exploitation of workers by a minority owning the main means of production, and that ruling classes lived by appropriating the surplus workers produced.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Said that in Chile the 'dictatorship' dimension was replaced by a different tactic, while the working class remains the social base.

collective-farming.rationale: Program organised expropriated land preferably in cooperatives and moved smallholdings toward cooperative work, while also giving personal plots and keeping small and medium private farmers.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Defined imperialism as the last phase of capitalism and blamed financial capital's search for profit for dominating poorer countries.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred: his program relied on taxes, and he proposed taxing the highest incomes, so he cannot have regarded taxation as theft.

positive-liberty.rationale: Said political freedoms must be made real by winning economic freedom, and distinguished abstract freedom from concrete freedom of those who are hungry or jobless.

total-state.rationale: Pledged respect for political freedoms, independent social organisations and religion, and said government control of the press would end press freedom.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Program warned against expansionist and revanchist impulses in neighbouring oligarchic states and called for negotiated settlement of border problems.

bound-labor.rationale: Program aimed to liquidate the latifundio, which it blamed for rural misery, and to give farmland to those who work it.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Wrote that the popular movement had always recognised the State of Israel and that his government would help consolidate its existence, while backing a peaceful settlement for Arab and Jewish peoples.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Said workers' directly elected representatives sit with state delegates on the boards of social-sector firms, and the program called for worker representatives on boards and production committees.

school-vouchers.rationale: Program had the state take responsibility for private schools in a single national education system.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: In 1973 he complained that Congress passed spending laws without financing and announced limits on money issue, though his government had run large deficits.

national-self-determination.rationale: Program made defence of peoples' self-determination a basic condition of international coexistence and recognised the right of colonised peoples to rebel.

force-without-un.rationale: Program and UN speech defend non-intervention and reject force and pressure by powerful states against weaker ones.

class-collaboration.rationale: Said his government rests on the existence of classes with antagonistic and mutually exclusive interests.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Said workers should become heirs to the inherited patrimony of techniques, knowledge, art and culture.

dominated-front.rationale: Told the UN that Third World states must organise collective action against neo-imperialism, and had Chile join the non-aligned declarations.

workers-nation.rationale: At the UN called on the international solidarity of workers to face the common enemy of imperialism, though his program also stressed national independence.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Said Chilean law discriminates against women and promised equality before the law, while adding that women also have the role of mother.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Program condemned all reactionary regimes that practise racial segregation and told the UN that Chile has no room for racial discrimination.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Said Chile's old legal order reflected the capitalist system and had to be changed to transfer power from the old ruling groups to workers, transforming the state's class sense.

national-mission.rationale: Quoted Lenin that revolution is not exported and that each people finds its own road, while presenting Chile's path as a new model of interest to others.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Said capitalist society instils 'machismo' by which men think they have more rights, that Chilean law sets inequality between men and women, and that the system discriminated against women in law, education and work.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Program charged that governments legislate for the few and promised an end to political traffickers, fabulous salaries and favouritism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Program had the state own the commanding heights, plan the economy and guarantee health, schooling, housing and jobs.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said the new society would have no first-, second- or third-class citizens and that everyone should have the same opportunity.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Held that Chile could build socialism by its own road and called it the first nation to do so, though he stressed international solidarity.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said his government derived from the freely expressed popular will and that popular sovereignty is the foundation of all power.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: His government expropriated land, banks and mines without owners' consent, under law, as part of its program.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Called for a society that outlaws the war of each against all in economic competition, in which creative capacity flourishes in favour of others.

separated-powers.rationale: As president he affirmed an independent judiciary and Congress, though the program put a single People's Assembly above the other organs.

vanguard-party.rationale: Said the parties of the Popular Unity guide the revolutionary consciousness of the masses, but called a single party of the revolution unrealistic.

priority-to-poor.rationale: His 1971 message and program made meeting the urgent needs of the great majority the first task, and the UN speech called for priority for education, health and the poorest.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Program guaranteed the right to strike and a strike ban appears nowhere in it.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Blamed poverty on the latifundio, monopolies and dependence, not on population growth.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Said that if the climate of terror continued he would limit individual guarantees, but otherwise bound himself to legality and the Statute of Guarantees.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Program promised to control prices of essential goods, and his government froze prices and a 1971 program point created supply and price boards; Wikipedia records that his government froze prices.

party-controls-media.rationale: Said that if the government intervened in the press, press freedom would end, and accepted constitutional protections for it.

party-commands-army.rationale: Insisted the armed forces are professional, subject to the constitution and not praetorian, and accepted a constitutional amendment making them non-deliberative.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Program limited high official salaries and ended fabulous pay and pensions of public officials.

recall-officials.rationale: Program stated that members of the People's Assembly and all representative bodies would be subject to voter control by consultations able to revoke their mandates.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Program called for reviewing and denouncing mutual-assistance and military pacts with the United States and denouncing the OAS.

people-in-arms.rationale: Called false the claim that he would replace the armed forces with popular militias and said Chile's forces are professional, 'the people in uniform'.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Condemned the US war that tried to stop Vietnam from reunifying as a single country.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Planned to renegotiate Chile's debt for longer terms and lower interest rather than cancel it.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Told the UN that national dignity and independence required nationalising basic resources and transforming the property system.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Planned to submit a new constitution to Congress and, if needed, a plebiscite, not to a separately elected constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Said it is a right of the Chilean people to pass through the transition without restrictions on political freedoms.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Said he would end private property where it harms others while keeping homes, cars and small enterprises.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Called the principle of legality an irreversible conquest and said there would be legality in the transition to socialism.

space-expansion.rationale: Said it is more just for great powers to 'put their feet on the earth' and deal with hunger and joblessness than to go to the moon.

leader-cult.rationale: Said he was not a messianic man or caudillo but one piece in the Popular Unity.

land-redistribution.rationale: Program and his policy expropriated estates above a maximum size for cooperatives and individual smallholders; he said agrarian reform would be fulfilled irrevocably.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Program called for solving border disputes by negotiation and warned against revanchist expansionism.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pursued Latin American integration through the Andean Pact and a Latin American organisation of states, citing the unity dreamed of by the founders.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Said historical change is determined by the social and economic factors a period has formed, and called Marxism a method for interpreting history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Program set out to end monopoly power of 150 firms that dominated industrial markets and nationalised strategic monopolies.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Program called to diversify exports, open new markets and keep relations with all countries.

moral-incentives.rationale: Hoped for a new man not moved mainly by money, promoted voluntary work and rejected a privileged worker aristocracy.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Said the guerrilla focus, armed insurgency or elections were roads peoples might choose according to their reality, and valued Guevara's dedication.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Program condemned all colonialism and neocolonialism and recognised the right of subjected peoples to rebel.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Said reformist and neocapitalist policies had failed and that capitalism's structure could not solve Chile's problems.

delink-world-market.rationale: Program called for diversifying exports, opening new markets and trading with all countries.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Program called for ending discrimination by sex or age in pay and condemned racial segregation and antisemitism.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Accepted and promulgated the Statute of Constitutional Guarantees entrenching rights as the price of taking office.

elective-rulers.rationale: Held that political authority rests on elections and the popular vote and sought to take office by election.

minority-veto.rationale: Program stressed respect for majority will and a political order built on majority support.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Program promised growing self-financing and rejection of aid and loans carrying political conditions; the UN speech said development rests on internal efforts.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Said the armed forces should not interfere in the political process and be non-deliberative, though he later invited officers into his cabinet citing constitutional order.

paid-care-work.rationale: Said housewives' work should carry social security and incorporated housewives into the pension system in the program.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Program and policy nationalised strategic industries and acted against ITT's hold on the telephone company.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Program made representatives subject to voter control, with mandates revocable through consultation.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Program unified social security under the management of the contributors within national planning.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Said his movement fights to free people from the vices of the consumer society and spoke of a 'society of needs' against it.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Program promised militant solidarity with liberation struggles but no record of his government arming insurgents.

corporate-influence.rationale: Accused ITT and Kennecott before the UN of trying to run Chile's political life.

job-guarantee.rationale: Program promised to guarantee work to all Chileans of working age and prevent dismissals.

non-intervention.rationale: Told the UN that non-intervention in a state's internal affairs is a fundamental principle of international life, and the program requires vigilance in defending it.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Program condemned antisemitism and racial segregation by reactionary regimes.

informal-organisation.rationale: Built his politics on mass parties, Popular Unity committees in every workplace and the CUT.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Held that disputes over nationalisation are the exclusive concern of Chile's own courts.

religious-nation.rationale: Described the movement as made up of atheists and believers, Masons and Christians alike, and promised respect for all creeds.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Said Chile would take neither a submissive nor a begging attitude toward the United States, and the program demanded full autonomy.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Said he would not end private property of a person's house, car or small firm, but only the essential means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Program and his government reinforced exchanges and friendship with socialist countries and restored relations with Cuba and China.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Said capitalism adds discrimination against women and tied women's drama to material conditions.

socialized-care.rationale: Program promised rapid expansion of public nurseries and kindergartens so women could work.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Said he recognised no alternative other than capitalism or socialism and criticised the Christian Democratic 'communitarian' regime as undefined.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Program promised to respect the rights of the legal opposition and his 1971 message recognised the opposition's political freedoms.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Program condemned every form of colonialism and neocolonialism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Program wanted people to gain a real role in state bodies through neighbourhood councils, workplace boards, committees and university government.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Said Chile faces a choice between capitalism and socialism, with no third option.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Called popular sovereignty the foundation of all power.

social-market-economy.rationale: Held there is no alternative between capitalism and socialism and aimed at a state-led transition to socialism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Program kept national armed forces, assured them equipment and pay, and defended them as professional and patriotic.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Program called for relations with every country regardless of ideology and his government adhered to non-aligned declarations.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Program promised to renounce commitments to the IMF, and he rejected politically conditioned loans.

property-franchise.rationale: Program called for universal, secret and direct suffrage for all men and women over 18, including illiterates and military.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Said that while media belong to oligarchic groups they deform popular interests, and that freedoms must be concrete and not only formal.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Said the principle of legality governs Chile and legality would remain in the transition to socialism.

racial-franchise.rationale: Program set universal suffrage and he told the UN there is no room for racial discrimination in Chile.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Program and UN speech argued that concentrated economic power in monopolies and transnationals threatens democratic life.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Program guaranteed free worship and respect for all religious beliefs and he welcomed the Church's role.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Program reorganised the police and reformed prisons for rehabilitation rather than abolishing either.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Program promised full civil capacity for the married woman, and he criticised her legal dependence on the husband.

rent-control.rationale: Program promised fixed rents capped at 10 percent of family income.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Called for dismantling foreign military bases and for ending the military pacts with the United States.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Said the old order lived on profit from owning firms and appropriating workers' surplus, and aimed to build an economy where work is the highest value.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Held that revolutionary violence is the legitimate response to reactionary violence.

independent-unions.rationale: Accepted constitutional guarantee that unions are free to pursue their own ends, and said the union organisation continues separate from management boards.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Said the aim is to transfer political and economic power to workers and the people.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Program kept hospitals, water supply and health in public provision and put transport in the state sector.

second-chamber.rationale: Announced he would put to the people replacing the bicameral system with a single chamber.

family-wage.rationale: The constitutional text he promulgated guarantees a wage sufficient for the worker and family, and the program fixed 'vital wages'.

person-over-state.rationale: Said the human being stands above both freedom and the economy, and called for a model centred on man and his needs.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Program gave regional and local organs powers but required them to stay within national laws and plans.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Program defined the armed forces' essential role as defence of national sovereignty and said he stood for peace.

free-public-college.rationale: Program promised state resources for universities and scholarships so workers' children could enter.

arms-reduction.rationale: Called for ending the arms race and for a disarmament plan to redirect military spending to development.

capital-controls.rationale: Program nationalised foreign trade and banking and attacked the flight of profits abroad.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Accepted a constitutional article making the armed forces and carabineros the only public force and criticised armed landowners.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Signed an accord with the CUT setting wages policy with union participation and promised wage commissions with workers.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Told the UN that the unfair economic order created at Bretton Woods must be replaced to benefit developing nations.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Said his government would build a new institutional structure not by violent destruction but by progressively superseding the existing order.

farm-price-support.rationale: Program promised guaranteed markets for all farm products, credit and cooperatives for farmers.

workers-own-party.rationale: Founded the Socialist Party of Valparaiso and built the alliance of workers' parties, arguing unity of the working-class parties was the key.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Program promised full civil capacity for married women and equal legal status of all children.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Distinguished formal democracy from authentic democracy in which the majority has real equality of opportunity.

women-suffrage.rationale: Said he was one of the signers of the law giving women the right to elect and be elected.

indirect-election.rationale: Program required every representative body to be generated by universal, secret and direct suffrage.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Program promised to humanise police procedure and guarantee respect for human dignity and physical integrity, and condemned past killings of settlers and miners.

close-ties-china.rationale: Established diplomatic and trade relations with China in January 1971 and urged its UN seat.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The program's first 40 measures ended the sales tax and ended tax increases on basic foods.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Program offered universal benefits such as free medical care, a daily half litre of milk for every child and free schoolbooks.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Led a multiparty coalition and called the parties orienters of the masses.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Program attacked statutes of privilege for big business and promised the state would stop creating new rich.

national-resource-control.rationale: Nationalised copper by unanimous vote of Congress and told the UN every state may control its resources.

multipolar-world.rationale: Called for a Latin American voice in the world, ties with the Third World and an end to the cold war.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Said the surplus is produced by workers and appropriated by owners, and put human labour as the highest value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Program fused national independence with the rise of the working people and he said patriotism means defending the people's interests.

notes: Answers rest mainly on his own speeches and interviews (marxists.org archive) and the Unidad Popular program he championed. He said in 1972 that workers would administer, not own, nationalised firms. Evidence on the 1972-73 economic crisis and on tolerance of armed leftist groups is contested and mostly not recorded as answers. He took office after accepting the Statute of Constitutional Guarantees demanded by the Christian Democrats.
